intro: Welcome to Cilicia — the coast the Romans won from the pirates. From the windy cape of Anemurium to Tarsus, where Cleopatra met Antony, ten ancient places are waiting. Choose a beacon, and let's go.
anemurium: Anemurium, the windy cape. A whole Roman town stands here, roofless, at the southern tip of Anatolia — baths, a theatre, and hundreds of vaulted tombs — staring across the water at Cyprus.
seleucia: Seleucia on the Calycadnus. One Corinthian column of a Roman temple still rises over Silifke, and the river is crossed where Vespasian's governor built his stone bridge in the year seventy-seven.
diocaesarea: Diocaesarea, high in the Taurus. Around the ancient temple of Zeus Olbios, Rome laid out a city of gates, colonnades and a theatre, twelve hundred metres above the sea.
cennet: The Corycian Cave. Two vast sinkholes the locals call Heaven and Hell. Here, the myth says, Zeus imprisoned the monster Typhon — and here, Strabo says, grew the finest saffron in the world.
adamkayalar: Adamkayalar — the man rocks. Eighteen figures carved into a canyon wall some eighteen centuries ago: soldiers, families at a funeral banquet, and one ibex. All nameless. All still watching.
korykos: Corycus. Rome kept a fleet here to hunt pirates. The castle floating offshore is medieval — but look closely at the walls on land: they are built from the bones of the Roman city.
elaiussa: Elaiussa Sebaste, the olive town renamed for Augustus. Its theatre, finished under Marcus Aurelius, seated some twenty-three hundred people on the hillside above the harbour.
kanlidivane: Canytelis. A town wrapped around the rim of a sinkhole some seventy metres deep, with a tower for Zeus, the tomb of a woman called Aba, and families carved into the cliff below.
soli: Soli Pompeiopolis. Pompey the Great settled his defeated pirates here and gave the city his name. Two hundred Corinthian columns once lined its avenue down to the harbour. Some forty stand again.
tarsus: Tarsus, capital of Roman Cilicia. Cleopatra sailed up the river to meet Mark Antony here. Saint Paul was born here. And the emperor Julian was buried here, just outside the city walls.
